references.text: In [ref:2 Krøn 15:6|2 Chronicles 15:6] we find a similar formulation: "People rose up against people, and city against city", which is an Old Testament background for Jesus' words that nations will rise up against nations.

In [ref:Jes 19:2|Isaiah 19:2] Isaiah prophesies that "Egyptian will stand against Egyptian, brother against brother, city against city, kingdom against kingdom" – a prophetic parallel to Jesus' words about kingdoms rising up against each other.

[ref:Matt 24:7|Matthew 24:7] is the direct parallel in the Gospel of Matthew from Jesus' eschatological discourse on the Mount of Olives: "For nations will rise up against nations and kingdom against kingdom."

[ref:Mark 13:8|Mark 13:8] is the parallel passage in the Gospel of Mark: "For nations will rise up against nations and kingdom against kingdom." All three synoptic gospels recount this statement from Jesus' end-times discourse.

In [ref:Åp 6:4|Revelation 6:4] the second seal is opened, and a red horse is sent out with power to take peace away from the earth so that people will slaughter each other – a fulfillment of Jesus' prophecy about war between peoples and kingdoms.
